info.title: Reassign REST API
info.summary: Read and write a Reassign day plan over HTTP.
info.description:
The public REST API for Reassign, the 24-hour circular day planner. It exposes the same engine the MCP server uses: read a day, create and move events, place work into free time, reflect on a past day, log moments against trackers, and manage areas, activity types, and the Inbox.

Public endpoints need a Bearer token, or the signed-in app session cookie, and generally Reassign Pro access. The 7-day free trial includes Reassign Pro. App-only projections instead require the session cookie, as marked on each operation. A token is either a Personal Access Token (`rsk_live_…`) or an OAuth 2.1 access token minted for the `https://reassign.app/api/v1` resource. Reads need the `events:read` or `events:write` scope. Write access includes read access; writes need `events:write`.

A span is `start` + `end`, two local datetimes "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" (no seconds, offset or Z) in the account's time zone, which a response names once as the top-level `timezone`. The end is after the start; an overnight or multi-day event simply ends on a later day. Dates are ISO "YYYY-MM-DD" and instants are ISO 8601 UTC strings. One occurrence of a recurring event has the composite id `seriesId@YYYY-MM-DD`, and a bare series id addresses the whole series; `scope: "future"` on an occurrence id also edits every later occurrence.

A path that no route serves, for example a removed route, first applies the same auth check, then answers 404 `not_found` "No API route has this path."; a Chrome extension build before 1.2.0 gets 422 `validation` "Update the Reassign extension to 1.2.0." in its place.

post.summary: Register, reconcile, disable, update, test or forget a device
post.description: Session only. `register` needs the Ably device identity token as ownership proof. `reconcile` disables the earlier accounts on the same installation, and its optional `name` (1 to 80 characters, for example "Chrome on macOS") renames the devices of this installation; `disable` stops this one. `activity` must come from a visible document. `test` sends one push to this installation, or with `id` to that owned device. Each device gets at most one test per minute. It returns `{ status: "accepted" }` (accepted by Ably, not shown). Without `id`, a device that is off or in its cooldown is a 429. With `id`, an unknown id is a 404, a device that is off or invalid is a 409, and a device in its cooldown is a 429. `device` changes one listed device of the user by `id`: `enabled: false` turns it off, and `prefs` sets its overrides (null clears them). Send at least one of the two. A device turns on only from itself, through `register`. `forget` deletes one listed device by `id` and returns the state without it. The device must be off, must not be this installation, and must not be in a send, else it is a 409. An unknown id is a 404. Every other action returns the current state. At most 120 requests per user per minute.

post.description: Place work into free time without computing slots yourself. Send 1 to 20 `requests`. Each request has a `name` (1 to 200 characters), an integer `durationMinutes`, and either an exact `start` or an `earliest` + `latest` window (local datetimes, at most 24 hours apart). The call is atomic by default: when a row fails, nothing is written and the other rows are `skipped`. With `partial: true`, the rows that succeed are written and the failed rows are errors. A request row that is not valid, for example one with both `start` and a window, has `status: "error"` with the code `validation`. Each row parses alone, so a row error names the field by its path inside the row, for example "`name`: Too small: expected string to have >=1 characters". Every request that succeeds books at once, and the row `result` has the `event`: an exact `start` books there when it is free, and a window books its top-ranked free slot. `autoCommitBest` is deprecated and has no effect. A taken exact `start` is a `conflict` row with `conflicts` and `nearestSlots`; send a slot's `start` as a new request to take it. A window with no free slot is a `conflict` row. `calendarId` and `mirrorCalendarIds` choose the calendars, and `mirrorStyles` sets how much each copy shows, as on an event create. Today, a start must be more than 5 minutes after now. A `requestId` makes a retry within 60 seconds replay the first result; a request without one is always new. A replayed row is `ok` with `replayed: true`, also when another row fails. Requires the `events:write` scope, which also includes read access. Returns `results`, one row per op with its 0-based `index` and a `status` of `ok`, `error`, or `skipped`. An `ok` row has the `result`, an `error` row has `error: { code, message }` (plus `conflicts` and `nearestSlots` on a conflict), and a `skipped` row has the `reason`. When something was written, the body has one `undoToken` and its `expiresAt`. When no op applied, the status is the code that the failed ops share (400 with `batch_rejected` when they differ) and the body adds the `error` envelope.

durationMinutes.description: How long, in whole minutes, e.g. 90.

areaId.description: Area id to attach (from the schedule read's `areas`); null or omitted leaves it unset.

activityTypeId.description: Activity-type id to attach (from the schedule read's `activityTypes`); null or omitted leaves it unset.

recurrence.description: Repeat rule as an RRULE, e.g. "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO"; omit for a one-off.

post.description: The one event write. Send 1 to 50 `ops`; each op names its verb: `create`, `update`, `shift`, `reflect`, `checklist`, `delete`, or `clear`. A span is `start` + `end`, two local datetimes "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"; the end is after the start, also on a later day. `update` with `start` or `end` moves the event, also to another day. A bare series id addresses the whole series, `seriesId@YYYY-MM-DD` one occurrence, and `scope: "future"` on an occurrence id that occurrence and the later ones. `calendarId` is the home calendar (on `create`, omit it for the account default calendar if one is set, else the dial only; on `update`, omit it to keep the current home; `null` for the dial only) and `mirrorCalendarIds` the one-way copies. `areaId` and `activityTypeId` take an id or `null`: on `update`, `null` clears the link and an omitted key keeps it; on `create`, `null` is the same as omitted. Calendar sync needs Reassign Pro. The 7-day free trial includes it. The batch is atomic by default; with `partial: true` it applies the ops that it can. A create returns `{ created }`, an edit `{ updated }`, a delete `{ deletedIds }`, and a clear `{ breakdown, items, truncated }`. A create, or an update that gives a series a new rule, adds `firstOccurrence` when the first real occurrence is not on the start day. A `scope: "future"` delete also returns the shortened series as `updated`. An edit of one occurrence returns that occurrence as `seriesId@YYYY-MM-DD`, with the original date, also when the edit moved it to another day. Requires the `events:write` scope, which also includes read access. Returns `results`, one row per op with its 0-based `index` and a `status` of `ok`, `error`, or `skipped`. An `ok` row has the `result`, an `error` row has `error: { code, message }` (plus `conflicts` and `nearestSlots` on a conflict), and a `skipped` row has the `reason`. When something was written, the body has one `undoToken` and its `expiresAt`. When no op applied, the status is the code that the failed ops share (400 with `batch_rejected` when they differ) and the body adds the `error` envelope.

post.description: The command bar over HTTP. `mode` is `"line"` (one free-form line, the default) or `"braindump"` (many lines). The input becomes events, Inbox items and logged moments, based on the schedule of the day, the taxonomy of the user and their AI rules. Then the command applies them. `apply: false` returns the plan and writes nothing. A question ("how much free time today?") gets its answer in `notices` and writes nothing. To link each new event and Inbox block to a web page, send `sourceUrl` (an http(s) address). To refer to an earlier line ("move that one later"), send `history`: the earlier `{ user, plan }` turns that the client keeps, with one line per proposed action in `plan`. History is context only: the model reads each history plan as a proposal that is not applied yet. The model returns the full updated plan, so `intents` repeats the proposals of the last turn that still hold, and the command applies them with the new line. A change that a turn applied is in the events of the day, so leave that turn out of `history`. The response has the resolved `intents` in the same shapes as the write ops (a span is `start` + `end` as local datetimes "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", a length is `durationMinutes`, a moment has `time`), `questions` that the client resolves, `notices`, `created` (each new event with its span, and each new Inbox block, with its `entity`, `kind`, `areaId` and `activityTypeId`), and one `undoToken` + `expiresAt` when something was written. The command refuses to delete a calendar-synced event or to move it to the Inbox. The command drops an intent with a value out of bounds and adds a notice. A `log_moment` rating outside the range of the tracker gets "A log was skipped because its value <value> is not from <min> to <max>." A new `park` item with a length outside 5 to 1440 minutes gets '"<name>" was not added to the Inbox because its length of <minutes> minutes is not from 5 to 1440.' When the model call fails, the response is 503 `internal`, not an empty plan. Needs Reassign Pro. The 7-day free trial includes it. Requires the `events:write` scope, which also includes read access.
